lines.text: Chapter one, section two. Scenario, the two-street clairvoyance game.
To isolate the effects of leverage from everything else, we revisit the clairvoyance game from volume one and simply add a second street of betting.
The setup is the same as before: each player antes a dollar and starts with three dollars behind, Opal is always dealt a King, and Ivan is dealt an Ace or a Queen at random.
Both players know each other's ranges perfectly, so the only uncertainty in the game is which card Ivan happened to receive on this particular hand.
The new twist is that there are now two betting streets, which we will call the turn and the river, but hands do not change value between them.
On the turn, Opal always checks, and Ivan can check or bet anywhere from one dollar up to his full three-dollar stack.
If Ivan bets and Opal calls a bet smaller than all-in, the river arrives, and Ivan gets another chance to check or bet whatever he has left.

In the one-street version of this game, the equilibrium was crisp: Ivan bets as large as possible with all his Aces, adds a proportional dose of Queens as bluffs, and Opal calls at a frequency that makes bluffing exactly break-even.
The natural question is what changes when we let Ivan fire twice, and the answer is that almost everything changes, in Ivan's favor.
As we work through the six questions in this scenario, keep asking yourself the same underlying question: how does the possibility of a future bet change what happens right now?
That is the pattern of thinking this whole chapter is designed to build in you.
